title: The Inventory Divergence
catchLine: "Three bullish draws. Flat price unmoved. Which signal do you trust?"
description: EIA shows a 4.2mb crude draw — the third consecutive bullish surprise. Brent barely moves. The desk has to decide whether the physical signal is real or already priced in, and whether to hold, add, or cut. A masterclass in reading divergence between inventory data and flat price response.

title: The Cargo Diversion Window
catchLine: "JKM opened $4.40 above TTF. The vessel was already loading. The desk had 4 hours."
description: An LNG cargo is mid-load at a Trinidad terminal, originally destined for the UK. The JKM/TTF spread widens sharply after an unplanned Japanese terminal outage. The desk runs the arb calculation — gross spread, freight rerouting cost, canal fees, buyer credit — and makes a diversion call under time pressure.

title: Crack Spread Compression
catchLine: "Crude spiked $6 in five sessions. The refinery margin collapsed. The desk saw it coming."
description: A geopolitical event sends Brent up $6/bbl over five sessions. Gasoline and distillate prices lag — and the 3-2-1 crack spread compresses sharply. Refiners begin cutting run rates. A crude desk that had read the forward curve correctly was positioned short the crack spread before the compression — with the P&L to prove it.

title: When the Dollar Spoke First
catchLine: "DXY strengthened 3.3% in 11 sessions. Brent's bulls were right — but three weeks early."
description: Three consecutive bullish EIA draws — and the price falls anyway. The US Dollar Index was strengthening quietly in the background, driving speculative long liquidation that overwhelmed physical buying. A cross-market read of DXY, COT positioning, and 10-year yields told the story before the price confirmed it.

title: Asian Utility Stocks Led JKM by Three Weeks
catchLine: "Tokyo Electric and KEPCO sold off. The LNG desk watched — and cut their long before anyone else."
description: Equity prices of Northeast Asian utility companies began falling three weeks before JKM spot prices softened. The desk running cross-asset surveillance picked up the signal — utilities cutting capex guidance implies lower energy procurement ahead. How one analyst's equity screen became a $2.1M short entry on JKM spot.

title: Iron Ore to Crude — The Chinese Demand Chain
catchLine: "Chinese steel output fell for the third consecutive month. The crude desk repositioned six weeks before the IEA confirmed demand softness."
description: Iron ore prices and Chinese steel production data lead crude oil demand by 6–8 weeks via the industrial activity chain. When iron ore futures on the Dalian exchange signal a production slowdown, refiners see weaker demand for crude before the official figures emerge. A step-by-step walkthrough of the leading indicator chain.

title: VLCC Rate Spike — The Arb That Almost Wasn't
catchLine: "The spread was $2.80/bbl. Then VLCC rates moved 40% in four sessions. Net margin: zero."
description: A Middle East Gulf–to–Asia arbitrage looked compelling at $2.80/bbl net margin. While the desk was arranging the vessel fixture, VLCC rates spiked 40% on news of Saudi Arabia increasing loadings. The arb closed before the cargo could be secured. The desk that got there one session earlier captured $1.8M. This one didn't.

title: Locking Freight Before the Rate Spike
catchLine: "Three VLCCs fixed at $38,000/day in February. Spot rates hit $56,000/day in April."
description: A desk that reads seasonal freight patterns correctly can turn freight from a cost into a revenue line. This case study walks through how a time charter position placed in the seasonal low generated $16,000/day per vessel when spot rates spiked — and how the desk managed the freight position alongside its commodity exposure.

title: Australian LNG Train Trip — 3 Hours to Position
catchLine: "The outage was announced at 9:47am. By 12:30pm, the desk had a position and a vessel."
description: An unplanned LNG train trip at a major Australian facility reduces expected loadings by 4 cargoes over three weeks. The desk assesses: magnitude of the supply gap, available Atlantic Basin replacement cargoes, the freight cost of rerouting, and JKM's likely response. A three-hour real-time decision log — with the full P&L outcome.

title: The Warm Winter That Moved TTF
catchLine: "European temperatures ran 3°C above seasonal average for six weeks. TTF fell 18%. The desk saw it in the weather data before the price moved."
description: Seasonal demand deviation is one of the most reliable commodity trading signals — but only if you track the deviation early enough to act before consensus catches up. This case study shows how a weather data workflow, integrated with storage levels and LNG send-out data, generated a short TTF trade entry 11 days before the market repriced.

title: The Position That Should Have Been Cut
catchLine: "The thesis was wrong by week two. The position was held for six. A $600K loss became a $4.2M loss."
description: The most instructive case study in the library — not because of the trade that worked, but because of the one that didn't. A Brent long built on a supply disruption thesis that resolved faster than expected. Six weeks of cognitive bias, missed stops, and escalating commitment. The full loss management failure — and what the desk learned.

title: The Basis Trap — Hedged but Not Protected
catchLine: "The position was 95% hedged. The desk still lost $1.8M. The differential moved — and the hedge didn't cover it."
description: A West African crude desk hedged a 1.2mb cargo with ICE Brent futures at 95% hedge ratio. The Brent flat price stayed flat. But the Bonny Light/Dated Brent differential collapsed by $1.50/bbl during the voyage — a basis move the hedge didn't cover. The mechanics of basis risk, why it happens, and how to manage it explicitly.
